requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
rationale:
The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.fingerprints`.

**Hash format.** `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` asserts a 64-character hex digest for the Rust case. This does not prove the digest is SHA-256. I treated the algorithm choice as owned by the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash` and did not assess it here.

**Words, whitespace and word boundaries.**
- `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` asserts `/// ab cd` differs from `/// abcd`.
- `string_literals_hash_as_words` asserts that `"ab cd"` and `"ab  cd"` hash the same and that `"ab cd"` and `"abcd"` differ.
- The bundled Rust case in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` covers the same split.

**Fingerprint scheme.**
- `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` runs `check` with the expected scheme `rust-structural-v1` for `languages::Rust`. I did not read the body of `check`, so I am assuming it asserts that scheme.
- `file_constructors_infer_the_language_and_return_addressed_contents` asserts `root.fingerprint_scheme() == "rust-structural-v1"`.

**Doc comments participate.**
- `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` asserts `/// Doc.` changed to `/// Docs.` changes the hash.
- `editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash` asserts the same for `Returns the count.` changed to `Returns the total.`.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` shows the doc comment is part of the item.

**Ordinary comments are excluded.**
- In `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments`, the `// {cite}` line comment above the item is changed from `a.b` to `c.d` with the hash unchanged.
- In the bundled Rust case, the block comment `/* note */` is edited to `/* edited */` or removed with the hash unchanged.

**Inner and outer grouping.**
- `inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups` shows that moving a word from an outer `///` into an adjacent inner `//!` changes the module hash. It also shows that splitting words across consecutive comments of one group keeps the hash.
- `reflowing_inner_and_block_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` covers reflow of inner `//!` and `/*! */` comments, and `/**` against `///`.

**Delimiters excluded and reflow preserved.**
- `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` covers `///` lines against one line, extra spaces and blank `///` lines, and a `/** * */` block with leading stars. It also asserts that changed or reordered words change the hash.
- `editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash` asserts that changing words changes the hash and that reflow does not.

**Attributes.** `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` asserts `#[inline]` changed to `#[cold]` changes the hash. `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` also keeps the attribute in the selected item.

These tests are marked with `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unmarked relevant test, no unassessed obligation, and no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
